subject: Recap & checklist: Hosted API suitability and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@brightcart.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & checklist: Hosted API suitability and next steps

Hi Alex / Sarah —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned: 

1) Deployment preference: BrightCart indicated a bias toward Hosted API for a rapid onramp (no infra changes, want to validate quality & latency before talking Dedicated or Private). We noted privacy-sensitive flows may later require VPC/Dedicated depending on compliance.

2) Trial scope & quickstart items (what we can stand up in ~48–72 hours):
   - Provision a staging API key and two endpoints (chat & embeddings) for BrightCart QA.
   - Default rate caps: 15 RPS across the account, 10 concurrent chat streams. Token budget: 250k tokens/day for the pilot (adjustable).
   - Sample prompt set and evaluation harness (BrightCart will share 50 sample prompts tied to two customer journeys).

3) Security & compliance asks you raised: SOC2 scope, data retention settings, and audit logging. I attached the security question spreadsheet you sent; we'll route to our security team for answers.

4) Next meetings:
   - Ops/SE call to map endpoints and throughput profiles (Marissa / Markus joining) — can you do Monday or Tuesday next week?
   - Optional short privacy discussion if you expect PHI-like fields; we can preview Private/Dedicated tradeoffs.

Can you confirm the sample prompt delivery timeline and pick a 30-minute slot for the ops call? Once you confirm, I’ll provision the staging API key and share endpoint URLs.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: BrightCart_Security_Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42 KB)
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@brightcart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightcart.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & checklist: Hosted API suitability and next steps

Thanks Ben — this is great and matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications: 

- We prefer Hosted for the POC because our infra team wants to avoid any on-prem lift for the first 6–8 weeks.
- Sample prompts: Sarah will export and share the 50 prompts by end of day Monday (06/07).
- Ops call: Tuesday 06/08 at 10:00 AM PT works for us. Please include any rate guidance we should expect in the staging env; we’ll validate latency and tail performance against our 200–600 token responses.

Also tagging Sarah (ops lead) — she’s primarily concerned about rate limits and burst behavior during checkout flows.

–Alex
Alex Taylor
Head of Product
BrightCart
alex.taylor@brightcart.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@brightcart.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & checklist: Hosted API suitability and next steps

Perfect — thanks Alex. I confirmed Tuesday 06/08 10:00 AM PT for the ops/SE call. Agenda I’ll circulate in the invite: endpoints + traffic profile, proposed rate caps, sample token budget, and evaluation success metrics.

Marissa / Markus — can you provision:
  - A staging API key for brightcart-stg
  - Two endpoints: /v1/chat/brightcart-stg (defaults: 10 concurrent, 15 RPS) and /v1/embeddings/brightcart-stg (defaults: 25 RPS)
  - A baseline latency SLO to log (p50/p95 targets for 512-token outputs) so BrightCart has something to validate against.

Marissa: I attached a short quickstart checklist (hosted-quickstart-checklist.md) that I’ll share with Alex. If we need tighter caps for the checkout spike, propose how we’d handle burst windows (short-term burst credits or canary routing to lower-cost model).

Alex / Sarah: after the ops call we’ll open a limited trial with those caps and share credentials + sample curl requests. If we see quality or latency issues, we’ll propose fallback policies to a smaller model for non-critical requests.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Ben

Attachment: hosted-quickstart-checklist.md (text, 3 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Ops prep for BrightCart hosted trial

Ben — quick internal note after reviewing the request. Action items I’ll own before the 10:00 AM call: 

- Provision brightcart-stg API key + endpoints as requested.
- Apply initial rate caps: chat 15 RPS / 10 concurrency, embeddings 25 RPS. Add a burst bucket: allow 30% burst above cap for up to 60s to emulate checkout spikes.
- Configure telemetry: enable per-endpoint token counts, per-api-key latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), and request sampling for content QA (10%).
- Security follow-up: I’ll attach answers to the BrightCart_Security_Questions.xlsx and include an audit log export example.

Notes for the call: suggest we run the POC for 10 business days, review metrics on day 3 and day 8; if BrightCart needs sustained throughput >100 RPS we’ll recommend Dedicated and provide a cost delta.

I’ll post updates to the HubSpot deal and drop the invite with the agenda.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
